russell-shaw.name: Russell Shaw
russell-shaw.bio: Russell Shaw is an English composer, sound designer and audio director whose game career began at Bullfrog Productions in 1992 after earlier work in recording and television audio. He scored titles including Syndicate, Theme Park and Dungeon Keeper before becoming a founding member of Lionhead Studios and composing for Black & White and the Fable series.

shahid-ahmad.name: Shahid Ahmad
shahid-ahmad.bio: Shahid Ahmad is a British programmer, composer, producer and games-industry executive who began selling games while still a teenager. His early work includes the C64 conversion of Jet Set Willy and the game Chimera; he later held senior production and developer-relations roles, including a long period at Sony PlayStation.

shaun-southern.name: Shaun Southern
shaun-southern.bio: Shaun Southern is a British programmer, designer, artist and musician associated with Mr Chip Software and Magnetic Fields. His career includes Kikstart, Trailblazer, Super Cars and the Lotus series; the CCG archive links his C64 music work to Hero of the Golden Talisman and Kikstart 2.

sid-meier.name: Sid Meier
sid-meier.bio: Sid Meier is a Canadian-American game designer and programmer best known for co-founding MicroProse and creating or leading landmark strategy and simulation games including Pirates! and Civilization. Although music is not his principal discipline, the CCG archive contains a recorded music credit connected with one of his early computer-game projects.

stefan-hartwig.name: Stefan Hartwig
stefan-hartwig.bio: Stefan Hartwig is a German composer and C64 scene musician who began creating computer music around the end of the 1980s. His work includes tracks connected with Turrican and Turrican II, and he later continued in professional game development and audio.

stephane-picq.name: Stéphane Picq
stephane-picq.bio: Stéphane Picq was a French game composer whose work became strongly associated with the French computer-game scene of the late 1980s and 1990s. After beginning as a programmer he concentrated on music, joining Cryo and creating distinctive scores for Dune, Lost Eden, MegaRace and Atlantis: The Lost Tales.

steve-barrett.name: Steve Barrett
steve-barrett.bio: Steve Barrett is an English composer and sound designer known for C64 and Amiga game audio. His CCG credits include Knightmare, SAS Combat Simulator and Tilt, while interviews and preservation records document a wider body of 8-bit and 16-bit music work.

steve-rowlands.name: Steve Rowlands
steve-rowlands.bio: Steve Rowlands is a British game developer whose credits combine design, graphics, programming, music and sound. He is particularly associated with the Apex Computer Productions games Creatures, Creatures II and Mayhem in Monsterland, with the first two represented in the CCG composer archive.

steve-turner.name: Steve Turner
steve-turner.bio: Steve Turner is an English programmer, designer and composer who founded Graftgold in 1983. His home-computer career combined code and music, with CCG-linked credits including Uridium, Gribbly's Day Out, Alleykat and Rainbow Islands.

tim-follin.name: Tim Follin
tim-follin.bio: Tim Follin is an English composer renowned for technically ambitious music on 8-bit and 16-bit systems. Working both independently and with Software Creations, he produced celebrated scores on the C64, Spectrum, NES, Amiga and other platforms before later moving away from full-time game composition.

timothy-brian-wright.name: Timothy Brian Wright
timothy-brian-wright.bio: Tim Wright is a Welsh composer and musician whose game career includes major work for Psygnosis. His Amiga credits include Lemmings and Agony, while later projects include the Wipeout series and music released under the name CoLD SToRAGE.

tommy-v-dunbar.name: Tommy V. Dunbar
tommy-v-dunbar.bio: Tommy V. Dunbar is an American musician whose early game credits include music for Archon, Barry McGuigan World Championship Boxing and Mail Order Monsters. Public biographical information about his games work is limited, so this profile avoids adding unsupported personal facts.
